title: CEO Autumn Update: Copilot for everyone and a 'Strong' year
author: P001
summary: Helena Marsh's autumn update to all staff covering 2025/26 results, the Ofsted 'Strong standard' outcome and the company-wide Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout.

blocks.p: *Published 21 October 2026 — Helena Marsh, CEO & Founder*

Hello everyone. Autumn is always the moment I look back at the academic year we have just closed and forward to the one we have just started. This year there is a great deal to celebrate, and one big change to get ready for.

blocks.h2: A record year for our learners

blocks.p: Our achievement rate for 2025/26 was **{{fact:achievement_rate_2526}}**, up from {{fact:achievement_rate_2425}} the year before. That is the single number I am proudest of in eleven years at Delcorn, because behind it are hundreds of apprentices who finished what they started. Thank you to every coach, tutor and support colleague who made the extra review, sent the extra nudge or rescued a learner who was about to walk away.

bullets: **{{fact:active_learners}}** apprentices are on programme today with **{{fact:active_employers}}** employer partners
Learner NPS over the last 12 months is **{{fact:learner_nps_12m}}**
**{{fact:epa_distinction_rate}}** of EPA results since 2023 have been Distinctions
Total revenue for FY2025/26 was **{{fact:fy26_total_revenue}}**

blocks.p: In February our inspectors judged us 'Strong standard' across every evaluation area of the new report-card framework. Siân and the Quality team have turned the feedback into our 2026/27 Quality Improvement Plan, with two priorities: getting every progress review done on time, and making sure the employer voice is heard in every review. You will hear more from Siân at the November all-staff call.

Since June, forty colleagues have piloted Microsoft 365 Copilot. They told us it saves them around two and a half hours a week — mostly on review write-ups, employer emails and meeting notes. The board has backed rolling Copilot out to every member of staff, and the executive team confirmed the go-live date of **Monday 9 November 2026**.

Before you get your licence you will complete the 45-minute *Copilot Essentials* module and read the AI Acceptable Use Policy. Aisha and Liam have also spent the autumn tidying SharePoint permissions so that Copilot only ever shows you what you are already allowed to see. If you spot something you should not have access to, tell the Service Desk straight away — that is exactly the behaviour we want.

blocks.callout: Copilot drafts; you decide. Nothing Copilot writes about a learner goes into Aptiva, an email or a review without a human reading and owning it.
blocks.title: The one rule to remember

blocks.p: This year we grow the AI Academy with the new Level 4 AI & Automation Practitioner programme, open our Birmingham hub, and begin the second year of our *Growing Together* strategy. I will host open Q&A sessions on 12 and 26 November — bring your questions, and your Copilot wins.
Thank you, all of you. Helena

title: Code of Conduct
author: P006
summary: Company-wide standards of behaviour for all Delcorn staff, associates and contractors, including conduct with learners, employers, conflicts of interest and use of AI.

version_history.change: Rewritten for fully remote working
Added professional boundaries with learners on social media
Annual review; added section 7 on AI use and section 8 on Meridian group obligations

blocks.p: This Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of everyone who works for or on behalf of Delcorn Learning Ltd, including employees, associate coaches, contractors, agency workers and non-executive directors. It applies whenever you are representing Delcorn — online, in a learner's workplace, at events and on social media.

The Code does not replace detailed policies. Where a specific policy exists (for example Safeguarding & Prevent, Data Protection or Anti-bribery), you must follow it as well. A breach of this Code may lead to action under the Disciplinary Procedure.

columns: What it does not look like
rows: Keeping review appointments, responding to learners within 2 working days, escalating concerns early
Cancelling reviews at short notice, signing off evidence you have not checked
Sharing resources, covering a colleague's caseload, giving honest and kind feedback
Gatekeeping information, blaming colleagues in front of employers
Accurate OTJ records, reporting data as it is, correcting errors promptly
Back-dating records, 'tidying' evidence before an audit
Checking AI output, protecting learner data, being open about AI use
Pasting learner data into unapproved tools, presenting AI output as verified fact

numbered: Maintain professional boundaries. Contact learners only through Delcorn channels (Teams, Aptiva, delcorn.co.uk email). Do not connect with current learners on personal social media.
Never accept money, loans or personal gifts from a learner.
Do not enter into any romantic or sexual relationship with a learner. This applies regardless of age.
Report any safeguarding or Prevent concern to the DSL the same working day using MyConcern.
Treat every learner fairly and make reasonable adjustments in line with the Equality, Diversity & Inclusion Policy.

blocks.p: Be honest about what a programme can deliver and about learner progress. Never misrepresent funding rules, eligibility or off-the-job requirements to win or keep business. Commercial commitments may only be made within the limits of the Scheme of Delegated Authority.

You must declare any interest that could, or could appear to, influence your judgement — for example a family member employed by a client, a second job with another training provider or a shareholding in a supplier. Declarations are made to your line manager and recorded by the Board Secretary in the Register of Interests within 10 working days.

bullets: Only access learner or employee records you need for your role
Store documents in the correct SharePoint library and apply the right sensitivity label
Never forward Delcorn information to personal email accounts
Report suspected data breaches to the DPO within 1 hour of discovery

blocks.p: Use only approved AI tools (currently Microsoft 365 Copilot and tools listed in the AI Acceptable Use Policy). You remain accountable for anything you send, publish or record, whether or not AI helped draft it. Do not use AI to make decisions about a learner's progress, eligibility or safeguarding.

As a member of Meridian Education Group, Delcorn follows group requirements on financial reporting, anti-bribery and modern slavery. Where group policy is stricter than this Code, the stricter standard applies.

If you see something that is not right, speak to your manager, the People team or use the confidential routes in the Whistleblowing Policy. Delcorn will not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith.

title: Whistleblowing (Speak Up) Policy
author: P011
summary: How staff can raise concerns about wrongdoing confidentially, including the Safeline Speak Up line and the non-executive whistleblowing champion, and the protections they receive.

version_history.change: Added independent Speak Up line
Updated for Meridian group reporting after acquisition
Annual review; named Fiona Gallagher as whistleblowing champion; response timescales shortened

blocks.p: Delcorn wants to hear about wrongdoing as early as possible. This policy explains how to raise a concern about malpractice, how it will be handled and how you will be protected under the Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998.

bullets: Fraud, bribery or financial irregularity — including funding fraud such as falsified OTJ hours, evidence or ILR data
Failure to comply with legal or regulatory obligations, including DfE funding rules or Ofsted requirements
Danger to the health and safety of any person, including learners
Safeguarding failures (individual safeguarding concerns about a learner go to the DSL — see the Safeguarding & Prevent Policy)
Serious data protection breaches
Deliberate concealment of any of the above

blocks.p: Personal grievances about your own employment (for example pay or a dispute with your manager) should normally be raised under the Grievance Policy instead.

rows: Your manager, or any member of the executive team
If you prefer not to go through your management line
Concerns about the executive team, or if earlier routes have failed
If you wish to remain anonymous
Concerns involving Delcorn's board or group matters

numbered: We acknowledge your concern within **3 working days**.
The Board Secretary and whistleblowing champion agree who will investigate within **10 working days**. Nobody implicated in the concern will be involved.
We aim to conclude investigations within **8 weeks** and will tell you the outcome as far as confidentiality allows.
All concerns and outcomes are reported anonymously to the Audit & Risk Committee each quarter.

blocks.p: Nobody will suffer any detriment for raising a genuine concern, even if it turns out to be mistaken. Victimising a whistleblower is a disciplinary offence. Knowingly making a false allegation is also a disciplinary matter.

We hope you will raise concerns internally first, but you may also contact a prescribed person such as the Department for Education (funding), Ofsted, the Information Commissioner's Office or the Serious Fraud Office.

blocks.callout: This policy is overdue for its annual review on 30 November 2026. The Board Secretary is updating it to reflect the new Meridian group ethics process.
blocks.title: Review due

title: Anti-bribery, Gifts & Hospitality Policy
author: P003
summary: Delcorn's zero-tolerance approach to bribery under the Bribery Act 2010, including the £50 gift registration threshold, £250 approval limit and rules on inducements to employers and learners.

version_history.change: Added rules on learner and employer inducements following DfE guidance
Aligned with Meridian group anti-bribery standard
Gifts register moved to SharePoint list; thresholds unchanged

blocks.p: Delcorn has zero tolerance of bribery and corruption. We will never offer, give, request or accept anything of value to improperly influence a business decision. This policy supports compliance with the Bribery Act 2010 and applies to all staff, associates, agents and non-executive directors.
DfE funding rules prohibit offering inducements to employers or learners to take up an apprenticeship. In particular you must **not**:

bullets: Offer employers cash, rebates, free commercial training or 'kick-backs' linked to apprenticeship starts
Pay or offer to pay an employer's co-investment contribution on their behalf
Offer learners gifts, vouchers or devices as an incentive to enrol or stay on programme
Pay recruitment or referral fees to employer staff for apprenticeship starts

blocks.p: Legitimate, programme-related items (for example a Delcorn notebook at an onboarding session, or assistive technology provided under learning support) are permitted.

rows: Acceptable if occasional and proportionate. No need to register.
Record in the Gifts & Hospitality Register within **5 working days** and tell your line manager.
**Prior written approval from the CFO** is required before accepting or offering, and it must be registered.
Any value from a party in an active tender or contract negotiation with us
Decline, or obtain prior CFO approval. Always register.
Cash or cash equivalents (vouchers, gift cards) of any value
Never acceptable. Decline politely and inform your manager.

blocks.p: Hospitality provided to public officials, including NHS and local authority employees, must always be pre-approved by the CFO regardless of value.
Facilitation payments are bribes and are prohibited. Charitable donations and sponsorship on behalf of Delcorn require CEO approval and must not be linked to any current or prospective contract.

Subcontractors, EPAOs and suppliers must be subject to due diligence proportionate to risk, and contracts must include anti-bribery clauses. Owners of supplier relationships are responsible for this check.

Report any request for or offer of a bribe to the CFO immediately, or use the Whistleblowing Policy. Breaches will be treated as gross misconduct and may be reported to the police and the Meridian Group Ethics Officer.

title: Branded Report Template
author: P027
summary: Standard Delcorn report template with guidance on structure, tone, accessibility and sensitivity labels. Replace the guidance text with your content.

version_history.change: Brand refresh — leaf logo and new palette
Accessibility guidance added; Copilot drafting tips

blocks.callout: Delete all guidance text (in italics) before you publish. Save your report to your own team's library, not to the Templates library.
blocks.title: How to use this template

blocks.p: *Three to five sentences a busy director can read in 30 seconds. State the purpose, the headline finding and what you are asking the reader to do. Write it last.*
*Why this report exists. Who asked for it, what decision it supports and any previous papers (link to them in SharePoint rather than attaching copies).*
*Lead with evidence. Every number should state its source and date, e.g. 'Aptiva, as at 5 November 2026'. Use tables for comparisons and keep charts simple — one message per chart.*
*Set out realistic options with costs, risks and impact on learners. Make one clear recommendation.*
*Link to corporate risk IDs (e.g. R04) from the Corporate Risk Register where relevant.*

bullets: Use UK English, plain language and the active voice
Headings must use Word heading styles so screen readers and Copilot can navigate the document
Add alt text to every image and chart
Write dates as 5 November 2026 and money as £12,500
Apply the correct sensitivity label: Internal by default; Confidential for anything with learner or staff personal data
If Copilot helped you draft, check every fact and figure against the source before circulating

title: Corporate Risk Register — October 2026
author: P011
summary: Corporate risk register as reviewed by the executive team on 14 October 2026, with inherent and residual scores, owners, controls, trend and a heatmap summary.

sheets.name: README
text: Corporate Risk Register — reviewed by the executive team on 14 October 2026 and presented to the board on 15 October 2026.
Scoring: likelihood (1–5) × impact (1–5). Inherent = before controls; residual = after controls.
Residual bands: Red 12 or above · Amber 8–11 · Green 7 or below.
Risk appetite (approved 15 Oct 2026): LOW for data protection, safeguarding and funding compliance; MODERATE for commercial and curriculum innovation.
Each risk has a single owner on the executive or senior leadership team. Next review: January 2027.

sheets.name: Register
sheets.sql: SELECT r.risk_id AS "Risk ID", r.title AS Risk, r.category AS Category, e.full_name AS Owner, r.likelihood AS Likelihood, r.impact AS Impact, r.inherent_score AS "Inherent score", r.key_controls AS "Key controls", r.residual_score AS "Residual score", CASE WHEN r.residual_score >= 12 THEN 'Red' WHEN r.residual_score >= 8 THEN 'Amber' ELSE 'Green' END AS "RAG", r.trend AS Trend, r.last_reviewed AS "Last reviewed" FROM risk_register r LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = r.owner_id ORDER BY r.residual_score DESC, r.risk_id

sheets.name: Heatmap
sheets.sql: SELECT likelihood AS "Likelihood", SUM(CASE WHEN impact=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Impact 1", SUM(CASE WHEN impact=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Impact 2", SUM(CASE WHEN impact=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Impact 3", SUM(CASE WHEN impact=4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Impact 4", SUM(CASE WHEN impact=5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "Impact 5", COUNT(*) AS "Total" FROM risk_register GROUP BY likelihood ORDER BY likelihood DESC

sheets.name: By RAG
sheets.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN residual_score >= 12 THEN 'Red (12+)' WHEN residual_score >= 8 THEN 'Amber (8-11)' ELSE 'Green (7 or below)' END AS "Residual band", COUNT(*) AS Risks, SUM(CASE WHEN trend='Rising' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Rising FROM risk_register GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY MIN(-residual_score)

sheets.name: By category
sheets.sql: SELECT category AS Category, COUNT(*) AS Risks, MAX(residual_score) AS "Highest residual", ROUND(AVG(residual_score),1) AS "Average residual" FROM risk_register GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC

title: Scheme of Delegated Authority
author: P011
summary: Matters reserved to the Meridian shareholder and the Delcorn board, and financial and contractual approval limits delegated to the CEO, CFO, directors and managers.

version_history.change: Limits uprated for growth
Shareholder reserved matters added after acquisition by Meridian
Refreshed for group thresholds (action A-2607-05); AI tool procurement added

blocks.p: This Scheme sets out who can make which decisions on behalf of Delcorn Learning Ltd. Authority may be exercised only within an approved budget unless stated otherwise. Anyone may refer a decision upwards; nobody may split a transaction to bring it under a limit.

blocks.h1: 2. Matters reserved to the shareholder (Meridian Education Group)

bullets: Acquisitions, disposals or joint ventures
New borrowing or guarantees above £250,000
Dividends and changes to share capital
Any single contract with a total value above £2,000,000
Appointment or removal of the CEO or CFO
Approval of the annual budget and three-year plan (after Delcorn board approval)

blocks.h1: 3. Matters reserved to the Delcorn board

bullets: Strategy, annual budget and annual financial statements
Contracts with a total value above £750,000 (up to £2,000,000)
Capital expenditure above £100,000
Unbudgeted expenditure above £50,000
Launch or closure of an academy or apprenticeship standard
Risk appetite statement and approval of Board-level policies (see Policy Index)
Appointment of executive directors other than the CEO and CFO

numbered: Any new AI tool that processes personal data requires a DPIA signed off by the Data Protection Officer before purchase, regardless of value.
Subcontracting of apprenticeship delivery requires board approval and DfE notification.
Settlement agreements require CEO and People Director approval.
Co-investment waivers are not permitted (see Anti-bribery, Gifts & Hospitality Policy).
All approvals must be recorded in Ledgerline or PipelineHQ with the approver's name.

blocks.p: Where an urgent decision is required between meetings, the CEO may act after consulting the Chair and, for shareholder matters, the Meridian Group COO. The decision must be ratified at the next board meeting.

messages.text: Morning all. People team ready with comms and FAQs. Jess has the Hub article and the Digest piece lined up for 30 Oct.
Confirmed: permissions remediation 100% complete. Salary auto-labelling live. All three board conditions met.
